title: Take the Expenses Quiz
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article proposes a simple team exercise for building financial literacy and ownership mindset: turning the organization's expense data into a guessing-game quiz rather than reviewing a spreadsheet directly. It argues that a static presentation of costs tends to feel preachy, while a game format engages people and reveals how little most team members understand about what it actually costs to run the enterprise. The piece describes how to structure the quiz, what kinds of questions work best, and how a small prize can boost engagement, closing with a call to make the exercise a recurring practice.
points: Reviewing an expenses spreadsheet directly with the team can come across as preachy or as a veiled request to cut costs.
Turning expense data into a guessing quiz makes financial literacy engaging rather than didactic.
The strongest quiz questions go beyond obvious costs like rent and utilities to less-visible spending categories.
A small prize for the closest guess (excluding finance staff) increases engagement.
Following the quiz with a discussion of which expenses most affect job satisfaction and profitability deepens the learning.
quotes: What it costs to run a business or enterprise of any size is typically lost on people.
A best practice to accomplish a deeper appreciation of expenses and to encourage team members to more fully grasp what it takes to operate the enterprise is to make a game out of the exercise.
The idea is to surprise people with questions and answers that will give them a more considered view.
Most teams delight in trying to guess the costs involved and become fully engaged in the quiz.
When people understand the expense side of the enterprise, they are better equipped to make decisions like they own the place.
